claims.text: Structural stability of near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles at high temperature is governed by surface-energy optimization.
Chemical stability of near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles at high temperature is governed by surface-energy optimization.
Structural stability of near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles at high temperature is governed by grain-boundary composition.
Chemical stability of near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles at high temperature is governed by grain-boundary composition.
Controlled annealing at 773–1173 K can alter nanoparticle grain-boundary composition.
Controlled annealing at 773–1173 K can alter nanoparticle surface energy.
Optimizing surface energy and grain-boundary composition enhances structural stability under high-temperature service.
Optimizing surface energy and grain-boundary composition enhances chemical stability under high-temperature service.
Nanoparticles with optimized surface energy and grain-boundary composition will be more structurally stable than nanoparticles without such optimization.
Nanoparticles with optimized surface energy and grain-boundary composition will be more chemically stable than nanoparticles without such optimization.
Catalytic operation is considered over 773–1173 K.
Thermoelectric use is considered over 473–1923 K.
